newsitem.title: USA: Maxco offers to convert common shares.
newsitem.headline: Maxco offers to convert common shares.

text.p: Maxco Inc said Tuesday it plans an offer to exchange up to 500,000 shares of common stock, at a price of $8 per share, for shares of the company's non-voting Series Five Preferred Stock.
The offer will be made to all common shareholders of record as of April 22.

The Lansing-based holding company said its board of directors approved a resolution that would allow it to offer common shareholders the opportunity to convert approximately 15 shares of common stock to one share of Series Five Preferred Stock.
Maxco Series Five Preferred shares will have a face value of $120 and will pay a dividend at the rate of 10 percent of face value per year, the company said.
The company plans to initiate the offer to exchange in June with a notice and information detailing the exchange sent to all common stockholders.

Maxco's Series Five Preferred shares are redeemable at the option of the company after the third anniversary of their issuance.The redemption rate is 105 percent of face value until the fourth anniversary, at which time the premium will decline 1 percent annually to 100 percent. The Series Five Preferred is non-convertible and non-voting.
At March 31, 1997, Maxco had 3,517,180 common shares outstanding and 62,345 Preferred shares outstanding.

Maxco's businesses include Ersco and Wisconsin Wire & Steel, both construction supply units; Pak-Sak Industries Inc., which makes polyethylene packaging; and Atmosphere Annealing Inc., a metal heat-treating service company. Maxco also holds investments in a real-estate development firm and in technology-related businesses, including Medar Inc.
